title: Calendars and timekeeping
summary: Five thousand years ago, Sumerians had a calendar of 30-day months, with the day divided into 12 periods. Egyptians, seeing that Sirius rose beside the sun every 365 days, near the Nile flood, devised a 365-day calendar that seems to have begun around 3100 BCE. Babylonians used a 354-day year of lunar months, and the Maya built 260-day and 365-day calendars. Calendars served religion, farming and government. Today's Gregorian calendar is a slight change to the Julian one.
